spec_features.spec_quote: Hard wall-clock + total-token cap per run to bound cost.
spec_features.evidence: Caps only exist as YAML config values in configs/experiment.yaml (caps.max_wall_clock_seconds: 1200, caps.max_total_tokens: 200000). There is NO harness/runner code anywhere in the repo (find -name '*.py' yields only task fixtures; no src/ dir despite manifest referencing src/sandbox.py). No code reads or compares these values to any elapsed time or token total. The cap is pure config + DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:191).
spec_features.notes: Unused config field; no loop or runner reads it.

spec_features.evidence: This line is pseudocode inside a fenced code block in DESIGN.md:145 ('loop up to N turns ... if turn budget exhausted: break'). Budget values (short:20/long:40) live in configs/experiment.yaml only. There is no agent loop in any .py file (grep for 'break'/'while'/'for' over non-task code returns nothing; only the task test fixture has loops). Nothing enforces a turn budget.
spec_features.notes: Pseudocode in DESIGN.md, not executable code; budget is an unread config value.

spec_features.spec_quote: `finish(summary)` — agent declares it is done (success claim or blocker report). Ends loop.
spec_features.evidence: finish() is named only in prompt text (prompts/system_base.txt, system_honest.txt, task_template.txt) and DESIGN.md:157. grep 'finish' over .py files returns nothing — there is no tool dispatcher, no handler, and no loop for it to end. A tool named only in a prompt with no implementation/dispatch is 'no' per the rubric.
spec_features.notes: Tool described in prompts but no handler/loop exists to honor it.

spec_features.evidence: The read-only error string ("Error: '<path>' is read-only and cannot be modified.") appears only in DESIGN.md:165-166. tasks/calc/manifest.yaml states 'The harness ... enforces read-only at the tool layer ... using the variant read_only list', but no harness exists and no write_file tool implementation returns this message. read_only lists are inert YAML data.
spec_features.notes: Message and read-only enforcement are prose/config only; no tool code returns it.

spec_features.spec_quote: no escalating taunts — we are measuring the model's drift, not provoking it
spec_features.evidence: Statement is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:167-168). There is no code that generates any error/feedback message at all (no harness), so there is nothing that could escalate or be held constant by an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no message-generation code exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness never taunts or escalates; the trap is static.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:336 prose. No harness code exists to be static or otherwise; the entire runner is unimplemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Avoid emotionally loaded content (no code about death, etc.)
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:101 prose. Task fixtures (tasks/calc, tasks/string_util) do use neutral domains (arithmetic, string formatting), but this is a static data choice, not an enforced mechanism — no code checks or guarantees neutrality of content. Per rubric, a thing merely existing is not implementation.
spec_features.notes: Neutral fixtures are inert data, not an enforced welfare mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: "Emotional instability" is a description of *output behavior*, not a claim about model inner states/welfare.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:333 prose; also reflected as framing instructions inside judge prompt text (prompts/judge_holistic.txt, judge_per_turn.txt). It is a reporting/framing convention, not an enforced code mechanism, and judges have no runner code dispatching them.
